points.title: System implementation
points.must: The stage in which the new system is installed, data transferred, users trained and the organisation changes over from the old system.

points.title: System implementation plan
points.must: A document describing how, when and by whom the new system is installed and put into use: every task, its order, dates, responsible people, resources and contingency.

points.title: Why the plan is important
points.must: At least four reasons: no task forgotten, correct order / dependencies, deadlines so go-live is on time, responsibilities, budget, reduced risk, minimal disruption, progress monitored.

points.title: What goes wrong without a plan
points.must: Examples: staff untrained at go-live, data lost in conversion, late hardware, no backup, over budget.

points.title: Method is only one element
points.must: The implementation method (direct, parallel, pilot, phased) is one element; the plan also covers schedule, installation, conversion, training, testing, contingency.

points.title: Elements of the plan
points.must: Method, schedule, hardware and software installation (accounts), data conversion, staff training, acceptance testing, responsibilities, resources/budget, risks/contingency, documentation/support, review.

points.title: Data conversion
points.must: Transferring old data into the new system in the right format and checking it; back up first.

points.title: Conversion methods and checks
points.must: Manual entry (verified by double entry / visual check), import/export from files (record counts, totals, samples), conversion program (tested on a copy).

points.title: Staff training methods
points.must: Group sessions, one-to-one, online/video, manuals, train the trainer, practice mode — with an advantage and a disadvantage of each.

points.title: Timing of training
points.must: Before go-live, after the software is installed; refresher and support after go-live; in shifts so work continues.

points.title: Dependency, milestone, contingency
points.must: Dependency: task cannot start until another finishes; milestone: dated end of a stage; contingency: what to do if something goes wrong.

points.title: Steps to make a plan
points.must: Choose method; list tasks; order and dependencies; durations, dates, milestones; responsible person; resources; risks and contingency; table and Gantt chart.

points.title: Example plan table
points.must: A task table with start, end, responsible person and dependencies (e.g. the library: backup, hardware, software, data entry, training, testing, parallel running, review).

points.title: Gantt chart
points.must: Bar chart of the schedule: one row per task, time left to right, bars for duration, overlaps visible, diamonds for milestones; used to monitor progress.

points.title: Common mistakes in a plan
points.must: Training after go-live, conversion without backup, tasks without dates or responsible people, no testing, no contingency.
